first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly, top to bottom on the iPad. The opening is plain English, not gushing, and I liked that it straight away said not every famous villa is what it seems. I didn't feel talked down to. By the end I knew far more about Nulla Ostas and room counts than I expected, but I still don't know a thing about deposits, contracts or who looks after Mum if she can't manage a boat.

journey.quote: Not every famous name on the lake offers it. Some are hotels that host weddings in their function rooms; some are heritage gardens with no bedrooms.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone telling us what to watch out for rather than selling a dream. That's the sort of thing I'd want from anyone handling our money.

journey.quote: Minimum nights, music curfews and standing capacity are rarely published. Get them in writing for your dates before you commit.
journey.reaction: Yes. In writing, before we commit. That's exactly what I'd tell Sophie myself.

journey.quote: Beds, not dinner seats, are the limit. Where they publish figures, these villas seat about 70 to 200 for dinner but sleep 12 to about 40, so most Australian guest lists need a nearby room block as well.
journey.reaction: Useful, and a bit sobering. So most of the family will be in a hotel somewhere else and being ferried back and forth. My first thought is the older ones getting back late at night.

journey.quote: Ask every villa on your shortlist the same question: which spaces are yours only when you take the whole property? Then get the answer in writing.
journey.reaction: Sensible advice. I'd have no idea to ask that, and it's the kind of thing that turns into a nasty extra bill later.

journey.section: Legal civil ceremony or symbolic ceremony on site
journey.quote: The Nulla Osta (a sworn declaration that you are free to marry) must be signed in person, by appointment, at the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Australian Consulate-General in Milan, with your Australian passport.
journey.reaction: This is the practical detail I want. It explains the foreign word and tells you where to go. I'll forward this bit to Graham.

journey.quote: The list runs by shore, not by rank: the western shore first, then two villas on the Como branch whose town we are confirming, then Bellagio and the eastern shore.
journey.reaction: You're the experts and you don't know which town two of them are in? That makes me wonder whether anyone from the company has actually been there. It reads like a draft, not advice I'd pay for.

journey.quote: "Confirm" means the official pages do not publish it; the open items are listed under each villa above.
journey.reaction: I appreciate the honesty, but after eight villas of 'Not published' and 'Not stated' I came away knowing what nobody knows rather than what I'd be getting. Fine if someone is going to ring the villas for us, a bit wearing to read.

journey.quote: Two names to keep apart: Villa Làrio and Villa Lario Resort in Mandello del Lario are different properties with different rules.
journey.reaction: Glad they warned me, because I would have mixed them up. Still, two villas with nearly the same name is the sort of thing that makes me nervous about paying a deposit to the wrong one.

journey.quote: Sereno recommends arriving by private boat and mentions helicopter transfers from Milano Malpensa.
journey.reaction: Helicopters and private boats. Lovely for the photos, but my mother uses a walking frame. Nobody on this page says whether she can get on a boat, up from a dock, or along a terraced garden.

journey.quote: | Villa | Where | Sleeps on site | Seated / standing | Min nights | Curfew | Ceremony on site | Private dock | Wet weather |
journey.reaction: Nine columns on an iPad. I had to pinch and scroll sideways and lost track of which row I was on. Half the boxes just say Confirm anyway.

journey.quote: one person who quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Australian dollars and in writing are the two things I was looking for.

journey.quote: On strike days, guaranteed services run only from 6am to 9am and from 5.55pm to 8.55pm.
journey.reaction: Very practical. I wouldn't have thought of Italian ferry strikes. Tells me someone has thought about guests getting stranded.

journey.quote: All eight villas have a dock, pier, jetty or pontoon, so guests and the couple can arrive from the water.
journey.reaction: Arriving by water is all very well, but what about the ones who can't step down into a boat? The road transfer is mentioned as a backup, but nothing about steps, ramps or how far it is from the car to the garden.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor holds the guest room block for you, with Wedded Privileges on every room your guests book.
journey.reaction: Holding the rooms is helpful. But what are Wedded Privileges? It's said as if I should know. A discount? A free upgrade?

journey.quote: None of the eight villas publishes an exclusive-use fee, so we have not printed one.
journey.reaction: Honest, I'll give them that. But I'm putting in a large sum and I'd like at least a rough idea before I get on the phone. The link to the cost article might help; this page alone leaves me guessing.

journey.quote: Ask which items (catering, music, staff) are included and which are billed on top.
journey.reaction: Right question, but where's the bit on deposits? How much, when it's due, whether it's refundable, whether the contract is in English and in what currency. That's the money I'm actually worried about.

journey.section: Shortlist your villas with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: They quote in AUD, agree their fee in writing before any work begins, and confirm inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the most reassuring sentence on the page. Fee in writing before work begins is what I need to see. I'd want the same said about the villa deposits.

journey.section: Shortlist your villas with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: With Wedded Concierge, you work with one Wedded Advisor from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: One person is good. But who? A name, a phone number, and whether they're in Australia or Italy. And who do I ring at 2am Italian time if something goes wrong on the day?

unanswered_questions: How much is the deposit for one of these villas, when is it due, and is it refundable if we have to cancel?
Is our money protected if a villa or Italian supplier goes under or cancels on us?
Is the villa contract in English, in euros or Australian dollars, and who checks it on our behalf?
Is Wedded Wonderland responsible if something goes wrong, or are we dealing with the villa directly?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong on the wedding weekend, at any hour, Italian time?
Which of these villas can someone with a walking frame get around: from the car or boat to the terrace, the ceremony spot and a bedroom?
Can older guests be driven right to the villa instead of taking a boat?
What travel or wedding insurance do you recommend, and does it cover elderly guests' medical issues abroad?
Is there a doctor or hospital nearby if an older relative is unwell?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked, and is the Advisor based in Australia?
Even roughly, what does a weekend at one of these villas cost in AUD?

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask which items (catering, music, staff) are included and which are billed on top.
turn_offs_found.why: The cost section talks about inclusions but says nothing about deposits, cancellation terms, contracts or currency risk. 'No mention of contracts, deposits' is exactly my worry, and for a page about committing to a villa this is the gap.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Villa | Where | Sleeps on site | Seated / standing | Min nights | Curfew | Ceremony on site | Private dock | Wet weather |
turn_offs_found.why: A wide, dense table on an iPad is hard to follow, and the villa lists are long runs of 'Not published'. Not tiny grey text, but tiring to read.

would_share_with: My husband Graham, with the Nulla Osta paragraph and the cost section flagged and my questions about deposits added
My daughter, to ask whether she has already spoken to a Wedded Advisor

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest count and the villas you have in mind, and we will tell you which are available on your date.
cta_reaction.why: The fee-in-writing and AUD promises make me willing. But I want to talk to a person, and the page doesn't offer a phone call or name anyone. I'd likely let my daughter fill in the form and then insist on a call before any deposit is paid.

top_3_changes: Add a short, plain section on deposits and contracts: typical deposit timing, refund and cancellation terms to ask for, contract language and currency, and exactly what Wedded Wonderland is responsible for versus the villa. Include insurance and who to call on the day.
Add accessibility for older guests: a question to ask each villa about steps, ramps, boat boarding and car access to the terrace, plus road transfers as the default for anyone with mobility issues.

Make the human side concrete and fix the unfinished bits: offer a phone call (not just a form), say who the Advisor is and where they're based, explain Wedded Privileges in one line, and replace 'town to confirm' / 'whose town we are confirming' with the confirmed town or remove that wording so it doesn't read like a draft.

Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing info listed under unanswered_questions
